audit.whatIsWrong: The page called this a 'Favoured matchup — difficulty 4/10' and gave Karma the 2+ items row, against a 28.57% win rate and a content layer that says 'you have no late-game answer to him'.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is Karma, Skill, Volibear x5. diff was already HARD but diffRating 4/10 and the summary line said Favoured — the page contradicted itself.
audit.corrected: Rows 2-6 flipped to Volibear on both layers; difficulty 8/10, carry threat 8/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: Phase whys claimed Karma owns levels 3-5 as a 'toll booth' and drifts to a winning 2+ items.
audit.why: Volibear's spikes are level 3 (Q's empowered run plus W's heal-on-recast together), level 6 Stormbringer (bonus health, disables your tower so you cannot kite under it), and tank items. Karma has no level-6 spike — Mantra exists from level 1.
audit.corrected: Rewrote phases[0..6].why around those three spikes.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no numbers and described Thundering Smash as a glow tell; the auto-reset, the W heal cooldown and the on-hit behaviour were all absent.
audit.why: Thundering Smash is 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s and is an auto-attack reset — the wind-up is the tell, not the cast. Frenzied Maul is a 5s cooldown that heals on the second cast against the same target and applies on-hit effects, so it scales with attack speed (his passive grants attack speed), meaning armour alone misreads the trade.
audit.corrected: Put the real cooldowns, the reset tell and the anti-heal trigger into breakdown.cooldowns, and the on-hit note into itemization.

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization said 'add anti-heal early into his sustain' without saying why it beats armour.
audit.why: Frenzied Maul applies on-hit and heals on recast; his damage rides attack speed from The Relentless Storm.
audit.corrected: Rewrote report[8].t to name the on-hit interaction and prioritise Grievous Wounds.

edits.before: Q poke at level 1 is among the best in the game — chunk Volibear on every last-hit and start the Mantra economy.
edits.after: Mantra is up at level 1 — RQ Soulflare chunks him before his Q stun or W heal exists, and it's the only stage you own.

edits.before: W tether threatens the root — anyone who steps to you early eats Q-W and donates the trade.
edits.after: He has Q or W but not both; your max-range poke works, but his bite heal erases it — even.

edits.before: Full kit: E shield-speed makes you untouchable in short trades. Mantra-Q (RQ) on cooldown gaps is a third of his HP.
edits.after: Q's empowered run-and-stun plus W's heal-on-recast close the gap and out-sustain your poke — the lane turns here.

edits.before: Spam the RQ slow-field on his farming spots and keep your shield for Thundering Smash (Stun) — the lane is a toll booth and you own it.
edits.after: Your Q rotations net nothing when his 5-second W bite heals them straight off, and Thundering Smash punishes every step forward you take.

edits.before: No new ultimate at 6 — your Mantra has been online since level 1. His spike is the danger window: respect it.
edits.after: Q stuns before Inspire can shield, and Stormbringer leaps in for bonus health while disabling your tower escape.

edits.before: First item amplifies the RQ chunk — keep him under 60% and the lane stays yours by default.
edits.after: Your first AP item sharpens RQ, but his bruiser items and W self-heal shrug it right off.

edits.before: You drift toward utility now — peel, shield, and speed your carries while the RQ poke softens objectives.
edits.after: He scales as a tanky brawler with no counter in your kit — one Q stun and he dives you or your backline.

edits.before: A toll booth he can't afford — RQ every step-up and tether the one chase he tries.
edits.after: Level 1 is the whole lane — after that his Q runs you down and W heals your poke off.

edits.before: Poke him off the wave and root the one mistake he makes. Thundering Smash (Stun) is the clock this lane runs on — read it before every step forward.
edits.after: Bank the level-1 chunk, then stop trading. Thundering Smash is 12s at rank 1 — his wind-up, not the cast, is your cue to be gone before it lands.

edits.before: - Volibear Thundering Smash (Stun): matchup-defining — The run-down stun — make distance the moment he starts glowing. It governs your forward steps. - E shield spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Thundering Smash: 12s at rank 1, 10s at rank 5 — it is an auto-attack reset, so the wind-up is the tell, not the cast. - Frenzied Maul is a 5s heal on recast: buy anti-heal or your chip nets zero. - Hold E for his all-in, never for poke.

edits.before: Open the toll booth: Q every last-hit, RQ the cooldown gaps, and hold E strictly for Thundering Smash (Stun). The lane is yours until he spikes.
edits.after: Level 1 is your one clean window: open RQ Soulflare before his Q or W exist, then last-hit at max range and hold E strictly for his Q stun.

edits.before: Start Doran's Ring + 2 pots. First: Malignance or Blackfire Torch into Sorcs; then Cosmic Drive / Zhonya's by threat. Add anti-heal early into his sustain.
edits.after: Start Doran's Ring + 2 pots. First: Malignance or Blackfire Torch into Sorcs; then Zhonya's. His W applies on-hit, so buy anti-heal before more armour.

I did not propose a new colour because I have no verified mapping of tone values to difficulty tiers; QA should set it to whatever the HARD tier uses.
